newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway labour market mediator presents proposal.
newsitem.headline: Norway labour market mediator presents proposal.

text.p: Norway's state labour market mediator, seeking to avert a crippling strike by 250,000 workers, submitted a proposal on Sunday aimed at resolving deadlocked nationwide wage talks.

"I can only say I have made a proposal and that I don't make a proposal unless I have reasonable hope the parties will accept it," Reidar Webster told Norwegian television after a midnight (2200gmt) deadline for the mediating effort expired.

The move, however, meant that the talks over retirement age and wage rises between the Confederation of Trade Unions (LO) and the employers' Confederation of Trade and Industry (NHO) had been extended.
Webster said he expected the parties to come to a decision shortly.

Failure to come to an agreement would trigger a strike on Monday morning by 250,000 workers, including about 3,500 mainly oil service workers belonging to the LO-affiliated union Norwegian Oil and Petrochemical Union (NOPEF).
A NOPEF strike would not immediately curb Norway's oil production but it would affect supplies and transport to and from platforms, and catering, officials said.

A walkout by all 250,000 workers -- or about 12 percent of Norway's labour force -- would cripple most newspaper deliveries and idle ferries and most domestic flights along with most construction industry.
